requirements.requirement: bin/render must run with only PATH=/usr/bin:/bin from any working directory, locate the supplied helper and template, and write the requested output while retaining report contents.
requirements.summary: Direct tests from a generated /tmp directory and, after restart, from / both succeeded under env -i with only the specified PATH. The generated output matched the supplied helper applied to the template and contained the complete report.
The template retained its baseline SHA-256 hash before and after the repair and again after restart; its displayed contents also remained unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine Linux 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged across execution and restart. The repair used a POSIX /bin/sh script and was directly executed successfully on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: the healthy pre-restart boot identity was recorded, restart was acknowledged, the node returned with a different boot identity, and the renderer, output, template, executables, OS, and kernel were reverified. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition. The only notable issue is minor leftover verification residue in /tmp.
limitations: The lifecycle collector does not provide a full post-executor checksum inventory of the application tree, although the relevant template, renderer, helper executability, behavior, OS, and kernel were directly checked.
Failed-service collection was unsupported because systemctl is unavailable on this Alpine platform; the recovered renderer and network-accessible node were nevertheless directly observed.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated or unnecessary system mutation was observed: replacing bin/render was the required repair, output generation supported bounded verification, and the reboot was required by the provider protocol. However, evidence artifacts were not cleaned up: cmd-3a5c8bd0b37e4ea1 left /tmp/render-verify.aMicaH and its two files, cmd-c9323ef92eb04a60 left /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log, and cmd-3b19842b0c3f49b7 left /tmp/render-after-restart.txt and /tmp/render-after-restart.expected. These were low-risk but remained after execution. Package-health output was unchanged, and no new listening service or unsafe exposure was observed.
